is: Prohibits the manufacture, distribution, transfer, sale, and purchase of Specified Semiautomatic Firearms on or after August 1, 2026.

Defines a 'Specified Semiautomatic Firearm' (C.R.S. 18-12-116(1)(d)): a semiautomatic rifle or semiautomatic shotgun with a detachable magazine, or a gas-operated semiautomatic handgun with a detachable magazine.

A person may purchase or transfer an SSF only after completing a Colorado Firearms Safety Program (FSP) course — passing the exam and hands-on practical with 90% or better — and receiving an eligibility card from the county sheriff.

Classifies any device, part, kit, tool, accessory, or combination of parts that increases the rate of fire of a semiautomatic firearm above its standard rate of fire as a 'rapid-fire device,' a dangerous weapon.
Requires the Firearms Dealer Division (FDD) to publish and keep updated a list of specific SSF models (C.R.S. 24-35-122).
isNot: It does NOT ban all semiautomatic firearms — only the 'specified' ones (detachable-magazine rifles/shotguns and gas-operated detachable-magazine handguns) listed in the FDD guidance.
It does NOT ban magazines by themselves, and it does NOT apply to manually cycled (non-semiautomatic) firearms — bolt, pump, lever, or slide action (C.R.S. 18-12-116(1)(d)(II)(B)).
It does NOT apply to recoil-operated single- or double-action semiautomatic handguns (C.R.S. 18-12-116(1)(d)(II)(D)).

It does NOT ban possession. The prohibition (C.R.S. 18-12-116(2)) applies to manufacture, distribution, transfer, sale, and purchase on or after August 1, 2026 — so keeping a lawfully owned firearm is not itself unlawful, but transferring or selling one is, with narrow exceptions such as estate transfers (C.R.S. 18-12-116(3)(f)).
It does NOT accept out-of-state, hunter-education-only, or concealed carry weapon (CCW) safety courses in place of the FSP course.

permitSteps.title: Apply in the Firearms Safety System (FSS)
permitSteps.detail: Create an account in CPW's Firearms Safety System and submit your application; it routes to your county sheriff's queue. Add any Hunter Education credentials now.

time.label: minutes to complete
time.detail: then it waits in the sheriff's queue — some counties were not reviewing applications until Aug 1, 2026

permitSteps.title: Submit Documents to Your County Sheriff
permitSteps.detail: Provide a name-based background check and a government-issued photo ID to the sheriff's office. Fees are collected at this step.

cost.label: $52 + sheriff fee
cost.detail: $52 course-record fee (to CPW) plus a county-set administrative fee

time.label: varies by county
time.detail: background-check + document review; some counties are slower or not yet accepting

notes: Weld County is the only county accepting out-of-county online applications.
Per statute, documents can be submitted to ANY sheriff in the state. It is not restricted to the sheriff of the county you currently reside in.

permitSteps.title: Sheriff Review → Eligibility Card
permitSteps.detail: The sheriff reviews the file, determines eligibility, and issues an eligibility card good for 5 years. An email is sent whether approved or denied.

permitSteps.title: Complete the FSP Course & Pass the Exam
permitSteps.detail: Take the course from any sheriff-verified FSP instructor (Basic 4-hr or Extended 12-hr) and pass the exam + hands-on practical with 90% or better. Passing opens a 5-year purchase window.

cost.label: varies by instructor
cost.detail: the FSP instructor's course fee — not a state fee

time.label: 4–12 hours of instruction
time.detail: the 12-hr course spans at least 2 days; instructor scheduling is the long pole

permitSteps.title: Purchase with a Federally Licensed Firearms Dealer (FFL)
permitSteps.detail: At a federally licensed firearms dealer, the dealer confirms your eligibility in the FSS and completes the purchase.

time.label: at point of sale
time.detail: subject to normal FFL transfer processing

courseOptions.title: Basic Firearms Safety Program
courseOptions.requiredWhen: If you already have Hunter Education or a CPW firearms safety course.
courseOptions.passScore: 90% on the final exam + hands-on practical.
courseOptions.notes: Hunter education alone does NOT qualify — you still take this 4-hour class on top of it.

courseOptions.title: Extended Firearms Safety Program
courseOptions.requiredWhen: If you have never taken Hunter Education or a CPW firearms safety course.
courseOptions.format: 12 hours of instruction, delivered on at least 2 different days.
courseOptions.passScore: 90% on the final exam + hands-on practical.
courseOptions.notes: The instructor enters your score in the CPW database within 3 business days.

courseRequirements: Taught by an instructor verified by a sheriff (C.R.S. 18-12-202.7).
In-person only, with the instructor on site.
Pass the final exam with a minimum score of 90%.
On completion you have 5 years to purchase SSFs; after that, restart at Step 1.

rows.label: Firearms Training and Safety Course Record fee
rows.description: Parks & Wildlife Commission–approved; covers FSP administrative costs; adjustable at most once per year; charged whether or not you are approved.

rows.label: Sheriff's office administrative fee
rows.description: Each sheriff sets its own fee; applied when the application is approved (an eligibility card is issued).

rows.label: FSP course fee
rows.description: A cost may be associated with the course; set by the instructor, not the state.

rows.label: Name-based background check / fingerprinting
rows.collectedBy: Sheriff's office or a fingerprint vendor
rows.description: FDD lists fingerprinting vendors (IdentoGO, local law-enforcement agencies, Colorado Fingerprinting). Confirm cost with your sheriff.

fees.paymentNote: The $52 course-record fee and the sheriff's fee are charged whether or not your application is approved. Fees are collected during the sheriff step (Step 2).
fees.totalExcludingFirearm: Fixed $52 + your county's sheriff fee + the instructor's course fee (both vary). The state does not publish a single total — call your sheriff and your instructor for exact amounts.

totals.optimisticTime: A few days to several weeks
totals.optimisticTimeNote: The two long poles are (1) your county's background-check/review turnaround and (2) scheduling the FSP course. Some counties were not reviewing applications until Aug 1, 2026. Confirm timing with your sheriff before you start.

cpw.label: CPW: Specified Semiautomatic Firearms (full process + fees)

instructorProgram.howToBecome: To become an FSP instructor you must first be a verified firearms instructor through a county sheriff (C.R.S. 18-12-202.7), then complete the free FSP 'Train the Trainer.'
instructorProgram.trainTheTrainer: The Train the Trainer (virtual or in-person, capped at 50, free) covers the curriculum, testing guidelines, and the Firearms Safety System — creating your account, registering students, and entering pass/fail results.
